extraction.name: MMMU
extraction.description: A massive multi-discipline multimodal understanding and reasoning benchmark for evaluating multimodal models on college-level tasks. It contains 11.5K multimodal questions from college exams, quizzes, and textbooks across six core disciplines.
extraction.creator: Xiang Yue, Yuansheng Ni, Kai Zhang, Tianyu Zheng, Ruoqi Liu, Ge Zhang, Samuel Stevens, Dongfu Jiang, Weiming Ren, Yuxuan Sun, Cong Wei, Botao Yu, Ruibin Yuan, Renliang Sun, Ming Yin, Boyuan Zheng, Zhenzhu Yang, Yibo Liu, Wenhao Huang, Huan Sun, Yu Su, Wenhu Chen
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Questions were manually collected/created by recruited university students (including co-authors) specializing in the subjects. Annotators gathered multimodal questions from textbooks and online resources, created new questions when needed, followed copyright/licensing rules, and were advised to avoid questions with immediately available answers. Quality control included duplicate detection with author review, format/typo checking by co-authors, and author-assigned difficulty categorization with very easy items removed.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: Quality control and error/annotation analysis included duplicate detection via lexical overlap and source URL similarity with author review, format and typo checking, difficulty categorization, and later analysis of 150 GPT-4V error instances by expert annotators; annotation error accounted for 2% of analyzed errors.
extraction.rai:annotatorDemographics: Over 50 college/university students, including co-authors, from various disciplines/majors; additionally, 90 college senior students were involved as subject experts for human evaluation.
extraction.rai:dataBiases: The paper notes that the dataset may contain biases from manual curation, and that models show bias toward textual information over visual inputs when evaluated on the benchmark.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: Limitations include possible bias from manual curation, incomplete coverage for testing Expert AGI, exclusion of some subjects due to lack of multimodal problems, and poor model generalization on less common image types. The benchmark is not sufficient by itself as a test for Expert AGI and lacks a direct mapping to the 90th percentile of skilled adults.
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: The benchmark is motivated by the societal importance of monitoring progress toward Expert AGI because such systems could substitute for skilled adult labor and create risks of job displacement and economic disruption.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: The dataset is intended as a benchmark for evaluating multimodal models' college-level, expert-oriented perception, knowledge, and reasoning. It includes a few-shot development set, a validation set for hyperparameter selection, and a test set for evaluation. The authors evaluate models in zero-shot settings and also report some few-shot results.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Data cleaning included duplicate detection using lexical overlap and source URL similarity, author review to remove duplicates, format and typo checking with standardized formatting corrections, and exclusion of about 10% very easy problems that did not meet design criteria.

name.evidence: We introduce MMMU: a new benchmark designed to evaluate multimodal models on massive multi-discipline tasks

description.evidence: MMMU includes 11.5K meticulously collected multimodal questions from college exams, quizzes, and textbooks, covering six core disciplines: Art & Design, Business, Science, Health & Medicine, Humanities & Social Science, and Tech & Engineering.

inLanguage.evidence: We introduce MMMU: a new benchmark designed to evaluate multimodal models on massive multi-discipline tasks

isLiveDataset.evidence: The live-updating leaderboard is available at: https://mmmu-benchmark.github.io/#leaderboard

rai:dataAnnotationProtocol.evidence: “we recruit over 50 university students, including co-authors, specializing in these majors as annotators to assist in question collection. They collect multimodal questions from major textbooks and online resources, creating new questions based on their expertise where necessary... The annotators are instructed to adhere to copyright and license regulations... the annotators are advised to select questions without immediately available answers... we perform two steps of data cleaning... reviewed by the authors... distributing the problems among different co-authors for format and typo checking... the authors categorize the problems into four difficulty levels”

rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis.evidence: “lexical overlap and source URL similarity are employed to identify potential duplicate problems. These suspected duplicates were then reviewed by the authors... distributing the problems among different co-authors for format and typo checking... the authors categorize the problems into four difficulty levels” and “We meticulously examine 150 randomly sampled error instances from GPT-4V’s predictions. These instances are analyzed by expert annotators... Annotation Error (2%)”

rai:annotatorDemographics.evidence: “50 college students (including coauthors) from various disciplines and subjects” and “we recruit over 50 university students, including co-authors, specializing in these majors as annotators” and “We involve 90 college senior students, selected to represent a wide range of experts in the corresponding 30 subjects”

rai:dataBiases.evidence: "MMMU, like any benchmark, has limitations despite its comprehensive nature. The manual curation process may carry biases"; "Additionally, GPT-4V often exhibits a bias towards text, prioritizing textual information over visual inputs"

rai:dataLimitations.evidence: "MMMU is not a sufficient test for Expert AGI, as per the definition [57], because there lacks a direct mapping between performance on MMMU and '90th percentile of skilled adults,' nor are college exams the only tasks an AGI shall tackle"; "The manual curation process may carry biases, and the focus on college-level subjects might not be sufficient for testing Expert AGI"; "we rule out a few subjects like law and linguistics because it is difficult to find enough relevant multimodal problems in these subjects"; "This indicates that the existing models are generalizing poorly towards these image types"

rai:dataSocialImpact.evidence: "Level 3, or Expert AGI, marks a critical milestone... leading to significant risks of job displacement and economic disruption. Therefore, it is of both intellectual and societal importance to closely monitor the progress towards Expert AGI."

rai:dataUseCases.evidence: "We introduce MMMU: a new benchmark designed to evaluate multimodal models on massive multi-discipline tasks demanding college-level subject knowledge and deliberate reasoning"; "The few-shot development set includes 5 questions per subject, and the validation set, useful for hyperparameter selection, contains approximately 900 questions, while the test set comprises 10.5K questions"; "Our evaluation is conducted under a zero-shot setting... We also report the few-shot results of some selected models in the Appendix"

rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol.evidence: “we perform two steps of data cleaning. In the first stage, lexical overlap and source URL similarity are employed to identify potential duplicate problems... eliminate any duplications. The second stage involves distributing the problems among different co-authors for format and typo checking... ensure adherence to a standardized format... Approximately 10% of the problems, classified as very easy... are excluded from the benchmark.”
